title: The Fourteenth Step
hook: The landlord taped one rule to the cellar door: count the steps every time. If you ever count fourteen... go back up. And don't look down.
lines: The cellar in my rental house has thirteen wooden steps.
The landlord taped one rule to the cellar door. Count the steps every time. If you ever count fourteen... go back up. And don't look down.
I laughed at it. Old house. Old man.
But I counted anyway, every night, going down for firewood. Thirteen. Always thirteen.
And my foot came down on one more step.
It wasn't wood. It was soft... and warm. And very slowly... it breathed.
I didn't look down. I backed up those stairs, counting every one out loud, and slammed the door.
Then I called the landlord. He was quiet for a long time.
Then he asked, How many did you count going back up?
He said, Then it isn't in the cellar anymore.
The line went dead... and under my chair, the kitchen floor took one slow, warm breath.
